title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook — Integration, Escalation, QBRs, Known Issues
author: Asha Patel
summary: Comprehensive playbook for enterprise onboarding covering integration checklist, escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, support process, and QBR / health check templates.
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the standard operating procedures for enterprise customer onboarding and ongoing support at Redwood Inference. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and SREs involved in initial integration, incident escalation, and regular health checks / QBRs. Follow this document for a predictable and auditable onboarding experience that aligns with our SLAs and enterprise commitments.

1) Onboarding phases and ownership

- Discovery (owner: Solutions Engineering)
  - Goals: confirm use case, success metrics, security requirements, and data residency constraints.
  - Deliverables: Integration Statement of Work (SoW), data access matrix, initial performance expectations.

- Implementation (owner: Solutions Engineering + Customer Success)
  - Goals: API access, network connectivity (if Private/VPC), model selection & configuration, initial test prompts.
  - Deliverables: Integration runbook, test corpus, traffic profile, and go/no-go checklist.

- Stabilization & Handover (owner: Customer Success + Support)
  - Goals: reach performance & reliability targets, finalize operational runbooks, schedule first QBR.
  - Deliverables: Handover document, monitoring dashboards, alert subscriptions.

2) Integration checklist (pre- and during implementation)

Pre-reqs (completed before first integration meeting):
- Signed contract and billing account provisioned.
- Admin users created in Console and API keys provisioned for SEs.
- Customer security questionnaire and network diagram provided.

Minimum integration steps:
1. Create customer API key and verify scope/quotas.
2. Exchange network / IP allowlist details for hosted vs Private deployment. For Private: verify VPN/Direct Connect or on-prem network details and test connectivity.
3. Confirm model selection and quantization profile (catalog model id + recommended config).
4. Upload initial prompt set and test corpus to shared secure storage.
5. Run smoke tests: authentication, sample generation, streaming responses, embeddings.
6. Validate latency & throughput using standard perf harness (see: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite).
7. Configure observability: route logs to customer-specific Kibana/Datadog workspace, enable token-level cost metrics for first 30 days.
8. Complete go-live checklist and schedule handover QBR within 14 days of go-live.

Configuration table (required values)

| Field | Required? | Example / Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model ID | yes | redwood/gptx-8k-v1 |
| Max tokens | yes | 1024 (adjust per workload) |
| Response streaming | recommended | true for chat apps |
| KV cache retention | recommended | session: 30 mins |
| Network mode | yes | hosted | private (VPC) requires CIDR and VPN info |

3) Support process & SLAs

Support tiers:
- Standard Support (included): email/ticket triage, business hours response for Sev 2/3.
- Enterprise Support (add-on): 24/7 paging for Sev1, named CSM, quarterly QBRs, runbook review.

Severity definitions and target SLAs:

| Severity | Impact description | Initial response SLA | Target resolution guidance |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Sev 1 (P1) | Production outage: inference unavailable for >50% customers/requests | 15 minutes (pager) | 4 hours for mitigation; permanent fix tracked in JIRA |
| Sev 2 (P2) | Significant degradation: high latency or errors affecting major flows | 1 hour | 1-3 business days for root-cause & workaround |
| Sev 3 (P3) | Partial impact: reduced performance or a single feature degraded | 4 business hours | Next release or configuration change |
| Sev 4 (P4) | Informational / minor bug / doc request | 2 business days | Planned in backlog |

Support intake and triage steps (numbered flow):
1. Customer raises ticket via Support Portal or assigned CSM.
2. Triage owner confirms severity using evidence (API traces, request ids, example payloads).
3. If Sev1, immediately page on-call SRE and escalate to Enterprise Support manager.
4. Assign owner (Support Engineer) and create reproducible test case.
5. If reproducible, implement temporary mitigation and notify customer.
6. Create internal post-incident JIRA for tracking and link to customer ticket.
7. Schedule postmortem if Sev1/2 with >1 hour impact.

Contact matrix (roles & channels):
- CSM: primary for customer coordination (email & Slack).
- Support Engineer (SE): ticket owner for technical triage (ticket system).
- On-call SRE: paged for Sev1 incidents (PagerDuty).
- Solutions Engineer: involved for integration/SDK issues.

4) Escalation playbook (detailed)

Escalation tiers and criteria:
- Tier 1 (Support Engineer): initial triage, reproduce, gather logs.
- Tier 2 (SRE / Runtime Engineer): performance issues, resource contention, kernel-level faults.
- Tier 3 (Engineering / Model Team): model quality regressions, compilation/kernel bugs, data residency/security incidents.

Escalation steps for Sev1 (example):
1. Support Engineer confirms impact and pages on-call SRE with incident summary and request sample.
2. On-call SRE checks cluster health: GPU utilization, queue lengths, preemption events, network connectivity.
3. If resource exhaustion, trigger autoscaling (if Dedicated) or failover to alternate region/model variant per routing policy.
4. If root cause is a model regression, open P0 engineering ticket with model onboarding lead and mark rollback as highest priority.
5. Notify customer via the agreed communication channel every 30 minutes until mitigated.

Escalation contacts (example placeholders — replace with customer-specific contacts during onboarding):
- On-call SRE (PagerDuty): pd:redwood-sre-oncall@example.com
- Enterprise Support Manager (email): enterprise-support@example.com
- CSM on-call (Slack): #cs-ashap

5) Known issues & workarounds (living list)

Format: issue id, short description, symptoms, workaround, status.

- RI-2026-045: Streaming stalls at ~512 tokens for some conversation patterns
  - Symptoms: client receives partial event stream and connection remains open.
  - Workaround: set max_chunk_size=256 on client and enable reconnect-on-stall. Back-end mitigation in progress (kernel patch scheduled in v1.12.3).

- RI-2026-088: High tail latency when KV cache growth >128 sessions per GPU
  - Symptoms: 95th/99th percentile latency spikes during batch bursts.
  - Workaround: enable per-customer cache eviction policy and reduce session retention to 15 minutes. Avoid large prefix caching for non-conversational workloads.

- RI-2025-210: Private deployment certificate rotation fails when intermediate CA chain missing
  - Symptoms: TLS handshake errors after cert rotation.
  - Workaround: ensure full chain is uploaded; use cert-validate script in onprem-packaging repo.

Maintaining the known-issues list:
- Support Engineers must add any customer-facing bug with severity >= P2 to this page and tag with 'known-issues'.
- Include a proposed workaround and expected ETA for permanent fix.

6) Health checks and QBR template

Health check cadence:
- First 7 days post-go-live: daily health check report (CSM + SE).
- Weeks 2-4: twice-weekly.
- Month 2 onward: weekly for 30 days, then monthly checks unless customer on Enterprise support where cadence is agreed in SoW.

Health check checklist (sample):
- Uptime (30-day rolling): target >= 99.9% for hosted customers on production routes.
- 99th/95th percentile token latency vs target.
- Request error rates (4xx/5xx) and root causes.
- Token cost per successful request and unexpected increases.
- Cache hit ratio and batching efficiency.
- Recent deployments and canary success rates.

QBR template (to present to customer)
1. Executive summary: health, major wins, risks.
2. Business metrics: usage growth, cost per 1k tokens, SLA compliance.
3. Technical metrics: latency percentiles, errors, top slow endpoints.
4. Operational: incidents since last QBR, mitigations, planned improvements.
5. Roadmap alignment and feature requests.
6. Action items and owners with due dates.

Attachables and supporting artifacts:
- Link to shared dashboard (Grafana/Datadog).
- Recent postmortems and incident timelines.
- Integration runbook and test corpus.

7) Post-incident and regression triage process

- For any Sev1/Sev2 impacting production, complete a post-incident review within 7 business days. Include: timeline, root cause, contributing factors, mitigation, and action items.
- For model quality regressions, tie regression alerts to a prompt-eval suite and block rollouts until a validation gate is passed (see: confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage).

8) Handover checklist for Support after onboarding

- Confirm support contacts and escalation contacts are recorded in ticketing system.
- Ensure runbook includes reproducible examples, expected behavior, and minimum required logs/traces.
- Confirm alerts and thresholds are set in metrics dashboards and Slack/Teams alert channels are subscribed.
- Share QBR cadence and initial 90-day plan with customer.

9) Templates and snippets (copy for reuse)

- Incident notification snippet: "We are currently investigating higher-than-expected latency on inference for model {model_id}. Our on-call SREs are triaging; we will provide updates every 30 minutes."
- Integration acceptance test command (curl):
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' -d '{"input":"Hello"}' https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate

10) Ownership and review cycle

- Document owner: Asha Patel, Customer Success (maintain and update).
- Review cadence: Annual review and after any Sev1 incident that required cross-team escalation.
- Reviewers: Diego Morales (SRE), Sofia Lin (Solutions Eng), Kavya Iyer (Support).

Appendix: Links and references
- Onboarding runbook repo: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding-runbooks

- Regression triage process: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage
